analytics.name: Analytic 1675
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Dead Drop Resolver by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application Permission via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]; Application State via Android Enterprise / EMM [Managed package inventory/status and package metadata]; Network Traffic Content via Enterprise Secure Web Gateway / Proxy [DNS/HTTP(S) inspection or proxy transaction metadata where enterprise decryption/inspection is deployed]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Per-app declared network destinations. Legitimate platform accesses (e.g., Slack app connecting to slack.com) should be in this list. Any platform access outside declared CDN is the dead-drop signal.
Apps approved for each public platform: social media apps for their own platform, productivity apps for their cloud storage. Non-platform apps accessing these platforms in background are anomalous.
Default 120s between dead-drop fetch and C2 pivot connection. Tightening: 30s — synchronous resolve-then-connect.

log_sources.name: android:EMM
log_sources.channel: Managed package inventory/status and package metadata

log_sources.name: webproxy:applog
log_sources.channel: DNS/HTTP(S) inspection or proxy transaction metadata where enterprise decryption/inspection is deployed

log_sources.name: mobile:DynamicAnalysis
log_sources.channel: Dynamic API/runtime trace: Background work scheduler or persistent service triggered the platform retrieval without user interaction
